long_biography.plain_text:
Tawera Group invested in New Zealand property from 1992 under a family structure that Mike Mahoney later chaired. One Auckland project converted an ageing office tower into 91 apartments, with the owner company ultimately controlled by Mahoney. The work paired property investment with adaptive reuse rather than a single repeatable building format.

Outside property, Mahoney spent decades restoring and racing classic boats. He learned to sail near Wellington and was still winning international regattas as an owner-skipper in 2024. He also helped introduce St Ayles community rowing skiffs to New Zealand. The flat-pack design allowed schools and community groups to build their own boats for coastal rowing.
